turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Hi! Here is one example.
We read. She reads.
Step: I see "she". So I add -s to "read".
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
Right: He sleeps a lot. Wrong: He sleep a lot.

Now you. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
turns.judgeInput:
KNOWLEDGE STATE (before this tutor turn):
Target form: thirdS. Learner level A1. First language Arabic.
W1 (wrong) strength 3: the verb does not change after he/she/it. Its error: leaves the verb unchanged after he/she/it ("She like tea").
W2 (wrong) strength 1: -s goes on every verb and -es/-ies are not needed. Its error: adds -s wrongly or misspells -es/-ies ("She watchs TV", "I plays").
C1 (correct) strength 0: add -s/-es after he/she/it. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: -es after sh/ch/s/x/o, -ies after consonant + y, no -s after I/you/we/they. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
